اسلام آباد : 29 اپریل 2026. وزیراعظم محمد شہباز شریف نے آج اسلام آباد میں وفاقی کابینہ کے اجلاس کی صدارت کی. وزیراعظم محمد شہباز شریف نے کابینہ ممبران کو پاکستان کی جانب سے مشرق وسطی' میں جاری کشیدگی کو کم کرنے کے لئے سفارتی کاوشوں سے آگاہ کیا. وزیراعظم نے عالمی سطح پر پیٹرولیم مصنوعات کی قیمتوں کے بحران کے باوجود عوامی سہولت کے لئے صورتحال کو ہر ممکن بہتر انداز میں سنبھالنے پر اظہار اطمینان کیا. وفاقی کابینہ کے اجلاس کے ایجنڈا پر موجود مختلف شعبہ جاتی پالیسیز کی بھی منظوری دی گئی. اجلاس میں ملکی سطح پر ویکسین کی تیاری کی پالیسی، ملک کی پہلی نیشنل ایگریکلچر بائیو ٹیکنالوجی پالیسی، نیشنل سیڈ پالیسی اور نیشنل سکلز ڈیویلپمنٹ پالیسی کی منظوری دی گئی. وفاقی کابینہ نے ملکی سطح پر ویکسین کی تیاری کی پالیسی کی منظوری دی گئی۔ اس تناظر میں DRAP کی زیر نگرانی قیمتوں کے تعین اور معیار کو یقینی بنانے کے لیۓ خصوصی کمیٹی کی تشکیل کی بھی منظوری دی گئی. پالیسی کا مقصد ویکسین کی مد میں درآمدات پر انحصار کم کرنا، قیمتی زرمبادلہ کی بچت اور ملک کو ویکسین کی تیاری میں خود کفیل کرنا ہے. کابینہ نے وفاقی نظامت تعلیم (FDE) میں یومیہ اجرت پر خدمات سر انجام دینے والے گریڈ 1 تا 15 کے اساتذہ کے حوالے سے سپریم کورٹ کے فیصلے کی روشنی میں انکی اہلیت کے مطابق FDE (Visiting Faculty) Regulations 2025 کے تحت انکی خدمات بطور وزٹنگ فیکلٹی لیے جانے کی منظوری دی. وفاقی کابینہ کے اجلاس میں نیشنل سکلز ڈیویلپمنٹ پالیسی کی بھی منظوری دی گئی۔ پالیسی کے تحت ملکی صنعت و تجارت کی ضرویات اور جدید دور کے تقاضوں کے مطابق افرادی قوت کی استعداد کار کو ہم آہنگ کرنے کے لئے عملی اقدامات کئے جائیں گے۔ مزید براں بیرون ملک جانے والے پاکستانیوں کے لئے بین الاقوامی معیار کی تربیت اور سرٹیفیکیشن کے لئے خصوصی اقدامات بھی پالیسی کا حصہ ہیں۔ وفاق اور تمام صوبے اس تناظر میں باہمی تعاون سے کام کریں گے. نجی شعبہ بھی اس پالیسی پر عمل درآمد کا اہم حصہ ہوگا. ملک کی پہلی نیشنل ایگریکلچر بائیو ٹیکنالوجی پالیسی کی بھی اجلاس میں منظوری دی گئی۔ اس پالیسی کا مقصد قومی غذائی تحفظ، زرعی پیداور میں خاطر خواہ اضافہ اور زرعی شعبہ میں تحقیق و ترقی اور مؤثر حکمت عملی کو یقینی بنانا ہے. اجلاس میں نیشنل سیڈ پالیسی 2025 کی بھی اصولی منظوری دی گئی۔ پالیسی کا مقصد غذائی تحفظ اور کسانوں کو بااختیار بنانا ہے. پالیسی کے تحت 15 سے 20 فی صد زرعی پیداوار میں اضافہ اور عالمی معیار کی سیڈ کمپنیز کے ساتھ شراکت داری کے لئے اقدامات اٹھاۓ جائیں گے. علاوہ ازیں وفاقی کابینہ کے اجلاس میں نیپرا کی سالانہ رپورٹ 2025 اور سٹیٹ آف انڈسٹری رپورٹ 2025 بھی پیش کی گئی. اجلاس میں وفاقی وزیر برائے تخفیف غربت و سماجی تحفظ عمران احمد شاہ کی والدہ کے انتقال پر فاتحہ خوانی بھی کی گئی. 32nd NITI Aayog In-House Lecture Series | Transforming the Mining Sector: Adoption of Modern & Advanced Technologies NITI Aayog organised its 32nd In-House Lecture Series on “Transforming the Mining Sector: Adoption of Modern and Advanced Technologies,” bringing together technologists, policymakers, and deep-tech innovators to deliberate on making India’s mining sector smarter, safer, and more globally competitive. Dr. V.K. Saraswat, Member, NITI Aayog, in his address underscored that critical minerals are as vital as bulk metals, noting that India’s resource base remains constrained and, as mining operations extend deeper, the infusion of advanced technologies becomes indispensable. Shri Ishtiyaque Ahmed, Programme Director, NITI Aayog, set the context for the session by outlining the strategic imperative of technology adoption across the mining value chain to enhance efficiency, transparency, and sustainability. The panel discussion, moderated by Dr. Rajesh Chadha, Senior Fellow, CSEP, examined key policy, capital, and technological pathways required to scale advanced solutions across India’s mining sector. Shri Suman K. Bery, Vice Chairman, NITI Aayog, delivered the closing remarks, emphasising that a technology-first mining sector will be central to achieving the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047, and that India’s innovation ecosystem is well-positioned to lead this transformation. #PMOIndia #NITIAayog #InHouseLecture #MiningIndia #CriticalMinerals #DeepTech #AI #MiningTechnology #Industry40 #ViksitBharat #DigitalTransformation

PRESS RELEASE Family Expresses Gratitude To All Who Participated in Buhari’s Burial and Prayers The most senior member of the Buhari family, the family of the late President, Muhammadu Buhari, Malam Mamman Daura has, on behalf of the family expressed gratitude to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and his wife, the First Lady, Senator Remi Tinubu for their role and that of Government of the Federation before, and after the passing of the former president. “It is truly comforting to receive such support from the President and the Vice President, Kashim Shettima, who went to the United Kingdom, and here in Daura, for the days he and the ministers during the mourning period. These have instilled confidence in all of us to face this loss with courage. “We are deeply grateful to the President on his thoughtful gestures in declaring a public holiday and renaming the University of Maiduguri after Buhari. “Our gratitude also goes to leaders of the various countries around the globe who either came in person, sent representatives, sent letters, or placed personal telephone calls to commiserate with us. Of special note were those of the King of England, King Charles III, the Secretary General of the United Nations, the Deputy Secretary General, Amina Mohammed, the Chairman of the African Union, and that of the Committee of Heads of State and Government of ECOWAS countries, and our former Head of State, Abdulsalami Abubakar. “Muhammadu Buhari’s demise is an irreparable loss and its pain is beyond words, but the general reaction and kind expressions give us the strength to cope with the loss of our esteemed family member and former leader of the country. “The family is equally grateful to Vice President Kashim Shettima in his own person and his wife, and to all state governors, especially those of Katsina, the host governor Dr Dikko Umar Radda; Professor Babagana Umara Zulum of Borno State and all those who visited us in the UK and Daura from Adamawa, Kano, Kwara, Lagos, Kaduna, Imo, Nasarawa, Bauchi, Sokoto, Kebbi as well as the several former governors, including Dr Peter Obi for their compassionate words of condolence. Your empathy has touched our hearts deeply, and we are truly grateful for your kindness. "We express our deep appreciations to former Vice Presidents Atiku Abubakar, Architect Namadi Sambo, Professor Yemi Osinbajo, and Ambassador Babagana Kingibe as well as to the President of Senate, Godswill Akpabio, the Speaker, House of Representatives, Honorable Tajuddeen Abbas, Deputy Senate President Barau Jibrin and the other leaders and members of the National and State Assemblies. “We do sincerely thank the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, SGF, Senator George Akume and his predecessor in office, Boss Mustapha, the current Chief of Staff, Honorable Femi Gbajabiamila and his predecessor, Professor Ibrahim Gambari, former and serving members of the cabinet in both administrations for their activities in these events and their comforting words. “We are very pleased with the amazing gestures of our traditional leaders, notably the Sultan of Sokoto, the Shehu of Borno, the Emir of Gwandu and the host emirs of Katsina and Daura, as well as the various emirs and chiefs from all over Nigeria and the neighboring countries who came in person or sent representatives. “We have been honored by the large turnout of religious leaders, Islamic, Christian and of other faiths, community leaders, women, youth and politicians of various leanings whose surge in Daura was both challenging and reassuring. “The family in Daura is also thanking past and serving security and intelligence, police and military leaders, permanent secretaries, and the rank and file civil servants, community groups and associations, civil society, and the media of communications. 1/2

29 years ago, the Chemical Weapons Convention (CWC) came into force — a major milestone in disarmament and the foundation of the OPCW’s work towards a world #FreeofChemicalWeapons. Why is the CWC a landmark achievement? 🔵 Near universal membership 193 States Parties — only four states remain outside the treaty, making it the most widely adopted disarmament agreement in history. 🔵 Concrete results As of 2023, the OPCW has verified the destruction of 100% of the chemical weapons stockpiles declared by States Parties — over 72,000 metric tonnes eliminated under international supervision. While verification depends on national declarations, the scale and transparency of this process represent one of the most substantial disarmament achievements to date. 🔵 Robust verification regime The OPCW conducts inspections worldwide, including at chemical industry sites, to monitor compliance and prevent rearmament.

Esto es incríeble. El Estado con un alto déficit fiscal tiene que sacar 5 billones para pagar sus pensiones mientras la plata sigue estando en los Fondos privados para que sus dueños multipliquen sus riquezas mientras el Estado tiene que dejar de pagar la deuda social por atender esos requerimientos. ¡Inaudito!. Y el Consejo de Estado, como siempre, en favor de las élites.

رہے ہیں ۔ انہوں نے وزیر پٹرولیم کی کارکردگی کو سراہتے ہوئے کہا کہ ہمارے اقدامات کی بدولت پاکستان میں خطے کے دیگر ممالک کے مقابلے میں صورتحال تسلی بخش رہی اور کہیں لائنیں نہیں لگیں۔ وزیر اعظم نے کہا کہ Defence Electronics Research Laboratory organised a one day exhibition on Counter Drone systems, ‘SAMRAKSHAK’ on 22nd April 2026, showcasing state of the art indigenous Counter Drone Technologies developed by various laboratories of DRDO. Dr Samir V Kamat, Secretary, DDR&D and Chairman DRDO graced the event as Chief Guest. Dr B K Das, DG ECS was the Guest of honour. DGs, Directors, senior officials from tri-services and MHA graced the occasion. The event brought together all the stakeholders including users, DRDO Scientists, Defence PSUs and industry partners. During his keynote address Secretary DDR&D and Chairman DRDO appreciated the efforts of various laboratories in evolving nobel counter drone technologies and systems to meet the paradigm shift in the game of warfare. He highlighted the importance of such events in bringing all stake holders together under one umbrella to discuss technologies and road map towards addressing emerging threat scenario. Dr BK Das, DS & DG(ECS) in his address emphasised the crucial role being played by Counter Drone Systems in the present geopolitical scenario and underlined the need to synergize all stakeholders towards meeting emerging challenges in this field. Counter Drone Systems/Technologies consisting of Radar by LRDE, Bangalore, RF Detection and Neutralization system by DLRL, Hyderabad, EO/IR Systems by IRDE, Dehradun, High Energy Laser Systems by CHESS, Hyderabad, High Power Microwave Systems by MTRDC, Bangalore, Acoustic Sensors by NPOL, Kochi and weaponized Drones by DYSL-AT, Dundigal were showcased during the expo. The event was attended by over 300 officials creating a platform for fruitful discussions and tangible solutions for meeting futuristic threat scenarios. The conclusion of the event was marked with the panel discussion of senior officials chaired by Dr B K Das, DG ECS, highlighting cutting edge technologies for Indian Defence Forces and the way forward for next generation counter drone systems leading towards Viksit Bharat.

🤝 CM Devendra Fadnavis presided over the signing and exchange of a revised MoU between the Government of Maharashtra (Water Resources Department) and National Thermal Power Corporation Limited (NTPC) for the development of Pumped Storage Projects (PSPs). معاونیت اقتصادی ریاست‌الوزرا می‌گوید که سیستم الکترونیکی مدیریت مکاتیب و اسناد اداری ادارات امارتی تأیید شده و به وزارت مخابرات و تکنالوژی معلوماتی هدایت داده شده تا آن را به‌گونۀ تدریجی تطبیق کند. در خبرنامۀ معاونیت اقتصادی ریاست‌الوزرا آمده‌است که جلسۀ نوبتی کمیسیون اقتصادی به رهبری ملا عبدالغنی برادر آخند، معاون اقتصادی ریاست‌الوزراء امروز (چهارشنبه) در قصر مرمرین برگزار شد. طبق خبرنامه، با تطبیق این سیستم هماهنگی میان ادارات دولتی تقویت شده، شفافیت، سرعت و امنیت ایجاد می‌شود، از جعل، فساد و ضیاع وقت جلوگیری به‌ عمل می‌آید، اصل ارقام دقیق و حساب‌دهی تقویت می‌شود و گام اساسی به‌ سوی حکومت‌داری الکترونیکی برداشته خواهد شد. در خبرنامه آمده که همچنان در این سیستم برای مراجعین نیز تسهیلات قابل توجه در نظر گرفته شده‌است. معاونیت اقتصادی ریاست‌الوزرا تصریح کرده که در این جلسه گزارش ۲۲ پروژۀ عام‌المنفعه نیز ارایه شد که از سوی رهبری امارت اسلامی در بدل عواید معادن، حکم تطبیق آن‌ صادر شده‌است. این پروژه‌ها شامل پروژه‌های ساختمانی، خط آهن و پروژه‌های انتقال و توزیع برق می‌باشد. #افغانستان #ادارات_امارتی #سیستم_الکترونیکی #Afghanistan #E_Government #Digitalization

وزارت صحت عامه می‌گوید که در جریان سفر وزیر این وزارت به سمنگان، بخش ۵۰ بستری نسایی ولادی در شفاخانۀ ولایتی این ولایت افتتاح و کار ساخت یک شفاخانۀ عمومی در ولسوالی حضرت سلطان نیز آغاز شده‌است. در خبرنامۀ وزارت صحت عامه که در صفحۀ ایکس این وزارت نشر شده، آمده‌است که مولوی نورجلال جلالی، وزیر این وزارت امروز (چهارشنبه) در سفر رسمی‌اش به ولایت سمنگان، بخش نسایی ولادی ۵۰ بستری را در شفاخانۀ ولایتی این ولایت افتتاح کرد. جلالی در مراسم افتتاح این بخش گفت که گسترش خدمات صحی از اولویت‌های اساسی این وزارت است و تلاش‌ها جریان دارد تا خدمات معیاری در داخل کشور فراهم شود، تا شهروندان برای تداوی مجبور به سفر به خارج نشوند. وی افزود که فعال‌سازی این بخش می‌تواند نقش مهمی در بهبود وضعیت صحی مادران و کودکان ایفا کند. خبرنامه می‌افزاید که وزیر صحت عامه در جریان این سفر، سنگ‌تهداب یک شفاخانۀ عمومی را در ولسوالی حضرت سلطان به ارزش ۶۴ میلیون افغانی نیز گذاشت. او ساخت این شفاخانه را گامی مهم در راستای گسترش خدمات صحی در سطح ولسوالی‌ها، کاهش مشکلات مردم و ارایۀ خدمات معیاری درمانی عنوان کرد. به گفتۀ وی، از میان ۳۱۸ ولسوالی کشور، روند تدارکاتی ۵۶ شفاخانه تکمیل شده و قرار است در سال ۱۴۰۵ کار ساخت ۱۰۰ شفاخانۀ دیگر نیز آغاز شود. جلالی گفت که این شفاخانه‌ها شامل بخش‌های جراحی عمومی، داخله، نسایی ولادی، تداوی اطفال و سایر خدمات ضروری خواهند بود و با تکمیل آن‌ها، ازدحام مراجعین در شفاخانه‌های ولایتی کاهش یافته و خدمات صحی در سطح ولسوالی‌ها بهبود خواهد یافت. در همین حال، والی سمنگان در این مراسم گفت که مسؤولین در چارچوب یک نظام مشترک فعالیت می‌کنند و با تعهد جمعی تلاش دارند خدمات بهتری به شهروندان ارائه کنند. در مراسمی که به همین مناسبت برگزار شده بود، ملا محمدشعیب رسالت، شماری از مسؤولین ادارات ولایتی، هیأت همراه وزیر و باشنده‌گان محل حضور داشتند.

🇷🇺🇬🇧 A "empty threat" Almost 100 Russian ships passed through British waters A month ago, Keir Starmer solemnly announced that British servicemen would henceforth be entitled to detain and inspect Russian "shadow fleet" ships directly in territorial waters. The headlines were loud. The reaction was also immediate - but not at all the one that was probably expected in London. Two weeks later, the Russian frigate "Admiral Grigorovich" passed along the southern coast of England, escorting two sanctioned tankers - Universal and Enigma - directly through the English Channel. The Royal Navy simply watched. No attempts were made to stop the convoy. Journalists from The Telegraph followed it from a ship off the coast of Dover - and wrote that it looked like a demonstrative response to the Prime Minister's threats. This was a clear signal: with a combat ship escort, the situation looks completely different. It's one thing to board a merchant ship without protection. It's another to decide on an incident with a military ship of a country that possesses nuclear weapons. Since then, the picture has not changed. In the month after Starmer's statement, at least 98 Russian ships under sanctions have already passed through British waters - about as many as in each of the three previous months. Of course, this has become a reason for pressure and criticism: analyst at the Atlantic Council Elizabeth Brow directly said that many have come to the conclusion about a "empty threat". The reasons are obvious. Britain does not have a specialized coast guard with law enforcement powers, like France or Sweden. The fleet is the smallest since the 17th century and is simultaneously engaged in several directions. Therefore, the legal and economic costs for now outweigh Starmer's desire to show his teeth. Although with increasing pressure and criticism, this may well change. And here it's important to return to the recent episode with the passage of the convoy through the English Channel. The fact that one frigate, escorted by two tankers, reduced the British's readiness to act is a vivid confirmation of the thesis: even a minimal signal of resistance is enough to stop the Western side. The British did not dare to have an incident with the "Admiral Grigorovich" - although without the convoy, they might have risked stopping one of the tankers to simulate toughness. ❗️But the lessons and signals are quickly forgotten. Therefore, the practice of escorting needs not only to be preserved, but also systematically expanded. To cover other routes - not only the English Channel, but also the waters of the Baltic, the North Sea, the Mediterranean, where French and Scandinavian patrols are actively working with the "shadow fleet". To use unmanned boats where there are not enough combat ships. To consider asymmetric options of pressure on those who seriously want to check Russian ships. rybar

Haryana is a land shaped by its history, its people, and its deep connection to the soil. From the sacred grounds of Kurukshetra, where ancient teachings continue to hold relevance, to its vast agricultural landscapes, the state reflects a way of life that is rooted, disciplined, and enduring. Its identity is carried forward through strong community traditions, local fairs and festivals, everyday crafts, and a food culture that is simple and closely tied to the land. In Haryana, culture is not curated, it is lived through daily routines and shared experiences. An initiative of NITI Aayog, Divya Bharat – A Window to the Soul of India is a curated national effort to showcase the country’s diverse cultural, spiritual, and natural heritage. Through a state-wise journey, it brings together India’s rich traditions, iconic landscapes, vibrant festivals, and living heritage, offering a holistic narrative of the nation’s unity in diversity. Defence Electronics Research Laboratory organised a one day exhibition on Counter Drone systems, ‘SAMRAKSHAK’ on 22nd April 2026, showcasing state of the art indigenous Counter Drone Technologies developed by various laboratories of DRDO. Dr Samir V Kamat, Secretary, DDR&D and Chairman DRDO graced the event as Chief Guest. Dr B K Das, DG ECS was the Guest of honour. DGs, Directors, senior officials from tri-services and MHA graced the occasion. The event brought together all the stakeholders including users, DRDO Scientists, Defence PSUs and industry partners. During his keynote address Secretary DDR&D and Chairman DRDO appreciated the efforts of various laboratories in evolving nobel counter drone technologies and systems to meet the paradigm shift in the game of warfare. He highlighted the importance of such events in bringing all stake holders together under one umbrella to discuss technologies and road map towards addressing emerging threat scenario. Dr BK Das, DS & DG(ECS) in his address emphasised the crucial role being played by Counter Drone Systems in the present geopolitical scenario and underlined the need to synergize all stakeholders towards meeting emerging challenges in this field. Counter Drone Systems/Technologies consisting of Radar by LRDE, Bangalore, RF Detection and Neutralization system by DLRL, Hyderabad, EO/IR Systems by IRDE, Dehradun, High Energy Laser Systems by CHESS, Hyderabad, High Power Microwave Systems by MTRDC, Bangalore, Acoustic Sensors by NPOL, Kochi and weaponized Drones by DYSL-AT, Dundigal were showcased during the expo. The event was attended by over 300 officials creating a platform for fruitful discussions and tangible solutions for meeting futuristic threat scenarios. The conclusion of the event was marked with the panel discussion of senior officials chaired by Dr B K Das, DG ECS, highlighting cutting edge technologies for Indian Defence Forces and the way forward for next generation counter drone systems leading towards Viksit Bharat.

In this episode of the All Things Policy podcast, Abhishek Kadiyala (@AbhishekSocials) and Brigadier Anil Raman speak with Soren Dayton (@sorendayton) about why the U.S. Congress has repeatedly failed to restrain President Donald Trump's military operations against Iran, even as the 60-day clock under the War Powers Resolution of 1973 continues to tick. The conversation examines the structural weaknesses of the War Powers Resolution and how it has failed to keep pace with shifts in military technology, constitutional interpretation, and geopolitical reality. Tracing legislative precedents from President Harry Truman's Korea to President Barack Obama's Libya intervention in 2011, the episode maps how successive administrations have exploited legal grey zones, with the Trump administration going further by filing only classified War Powers reports. Despite warnings from Republican Senators John Curtis and Mike Rounds about the 60-day limit, the episode argues that the real obstacle is political will, not legal ambiguity. The episode ultimately asks whether the War Powers Resolution has become less a constraint on executive power and more a permission slip for it, and what a genuinely reformed version of the law would need to look like. وزارت آب و انرژی از آغاز پروژۀ انتقال و توزیع برق در ولسوالی‌های قوش‌تپه و درزاب ولایت جوزجان به ارزش ۱.۶ میلیارد افغانی خبر داده‌است که با تکمیل آن، حدود ۹۰هزار تن از باشنده‌گان این مناطق از انرژی برق مستفید خواهند شد. براساس معلومات این وزارت، این پروژه با هزینۀ مجموعی یک میلیارد و ۶۰۰میلیون افغانی تمویل می‌شود و کار تطبیق آن را شرکت«State Corps» به عهده دارد. مولوی محمدیونس آخندزاده، وزیر آب و انرژی امروز (چهارشنبه) در مراسم آغاز کار این پروژه گفت که در چارچوب آن، برق از سب‌استیشن مرکزی تا ولسوالی‌های درزاب و قوش‌تپه به‌طول مجموعی ۸۵ کیلومتر انتقال داده می‌شود. وی افزود که در این پروژه دو سب‌استیشن جدید در این ولسوالی‌ها اعمار خواهد شد و شبکۀ توزیع برق نیز در هر دو ولسوالی ایجاد می‌گردد. از سوی دیگر، انجنیر علاوالدین سلیم، معاون شرکت «State Corps» می‌گوید که بخش نخست پروژه شامل انتقال لین برق ۲۲۰کیلوولت به ولسوالی قوش‌تپه و سپس تا ولسوالی درزاب است که در مجموع حدود ۸۸کیلومتر لین انتقالی و توزیعی را در بر می‌گیرد. به گفتۀ او، بخش دوم پروژه شامل اعمار دو سب‌استیشن است که نقش اساسی در تنظیم و توزیع انرژی برق خواهد داشت. وی افزود که با تکمیل پروژه، حدود ۹۰هزار تن از باشنده‌گان این دو ولسوالی از برق مستفید شده و زمینۀ بهبود وضعیت اقتصادی و رفاه اجتماعی آنان فراهم می‌شود. مولوی عبدالله سرحدی، والی جوزجان در این مراسم گفت: «با تأمین امنیت سراسری و ایجاد فضای مناسب کاری در سایه امارت اسلامی، زمینۀ تطبیق چنین پروژه‌های بزرگ فراهم شده‌است.» او افزود که با افتتاح این پروژه، باشنده‌گان قوش‌تپه و درزاب از سهولت‌های اساسی و برق پایدار بهره‌مند خواهند شد. در همین حال، شماری از باشنده‌گان محل می‌گویند که با انتقال برق به این مناطق، بخش زیادی از مشکلات زنده‌گی آنان حل خواهد شد. صبغت‌الله، یکی از باشنده‌گان ولسوالی قوش‌تپه گفت که نبود برق مشکلات زیادی را برای مردم ایجاد کرده‌است. وی افزود: «اکنون با تکمیل این پروژه، فرزندان ما می‌توانند در روشنایی درس بخوانند و آیندۀ بهتری داشته باشند.» گفته می‌شود که کار این پروژه در مدت سه سال تکمیل و به بهره‌برداری سپرده خواهد شد.

فدراسین فوتبال افغانستان می‌گوید که سی‌وششمین کنگرۀ سالانۀ کنفدراسیون فوتبال آسیا با حضور محمدیوسف کارگر، رئیس و بهرام صدیقی، سکرترجنرال این فدراسیون در شهر ونکوور کانادا برگزار شد. فدراسین فوتبال افغانستان با نشر خبرنامه‌ای نوشته‌است که در این نشست، برنامه‌های توسعۀ فوتبال در آسیا، گزارش‌های فنی و مالی و راه‌های تقویت زیرساخت‌های ورزشی مورد بررسی قرار گرفت. در خبرنامه آمده که همچنان از ۹ کشور آسیایی که موفق به صعود به رقابت‌های جام جهانی ۲۰۲۶ شده‌اند، به ‌صورت ویژه تقدیر شد؛ اقدامی که بیانگر جایگاه روبه‌رشد فوتبال آسیا در سطح جهانی است. طبق خبرنامه، هیأت فدراسیون فوتبال افغانستان با حضور فعال در این کنگره، نقش قابل توجهی در طرح مسایل توسعه‌ای فوتبال کشور ایفا کرد. محمدیوسف کارگر در این نشست بر آغاز فوری پروژه‌های زیربنایی ورزشی در ولایت‌های مختلف افغانستان تأکید کرده‌است. وی همچنین خواهان همکاری گستردۀ کنفدراسیون فوتبال آسیا در زمینۀ ارتقای ظرفیت‌های فنی و تخنیکی مربیان و داوران در رشته‌های فوتبال، فوتسال و فوتبال ساحلی شد تا روند حرفه‌ای‌سازی ورزش در افغانستان سرعت بیشتری بگیرد. رهبری کنفدراسیون فوتبال آسیا تعهد کرده‌است که حمایت همه‌جانبه‌ای در بخش توسعه زیرساخت‌ها و برنامه‌های آموزشی ارایه خواهد کرد. #فوتبال #آسیا #کنگره #Football #AFC #Congress

Kyiv has proposed to its partners assisting Ukraine a separate cooperation format called “Drone Deals”—special agreements regarding the production and supply of Ukrainian drones, missiles, shells, and other types of weapons, military equipment, and software; integration with partners’ defense systems; as well as the provision of expertise and technology exchange. Volodymyr Zelenskyy / Володимир Зеленський (@ZelenskyyUa) I held an expanded meeting on key issues related to the export of Ukrainian weapons. The export of Ukrainian weapons will become a reality – we have approved all the details at the level of our state institutions. Currently, our security expertise and weapons, which have been tested in modern warfare, are of interest to all partners capable of ensuring a real level of protection for their statehood and the lives of their citizens. We have proposed to partners who support Ukraine a special format of cooperation – Drone Deals – special agreements on the production and supply of our drones, missiles, ammunition, and other in-demand types of weapons, military equipment, software, integration with partners’ defense systems, as well as the provision of our expertise and the technological exchange needed by Ukraine. Today, I approved the areas for this interstate work and the development of automatic permits for businesses regarding arms exports. The algorithm is absolutely clear: at the interstate level, based on the principle of reciprocity, we define the framework for security cooperation through the relevant agreement. Then the process continues at the level of state institutions and manufacturers. We are simplifying bureaucratic procedures, maintaining an adequate level of export control, and launching practical operating mechanisms for companies. Ukrainian companies will receive a real opportunity to enter partner countries’ markets, provided that our military has the right to receive the necessary volume of weapons first. A surplus of production capacity in Ukraine for certain types of weapons reaches 50 per cent, and this is a direct result of our state investment in Ukraine’s defense industry and our cooperation with partners. I instructed the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, together with our intelligence services and the Security Service of Ukraine, to determine the list of countries to which exports of our weapons are not possible due to their cooperation with the aggressor state. This is a serious challenge – to prevent our technologies and weapons from falling into Russian hands. The National Security and Defense Council of Ukraine will coordinate export processes and act as a guarantor that the needs of Ukraine’s Defense and Security Forces are met first, while only surplus production – what manufacturers can produce beyond the state order in Ukraine – will be exported. The Ministry of Defense of Ukraine and the General Staff will determine the required volumes for the needs of our Defense Forces. I have instructed government officials and the National Security and Defense Council of Ukraine to present to the public the necessary information on the details of our weapons export process. The US is stepping back from the Pacific. China is stepping in. And India? Still figuring out where it stands in a region that covers 15% of the Earth's surface. The argument is sharp: — The 2025 Quad Leaders' Summit collapsed because Trump refused to attend — The US opened protected Pacific marine zones to commercial fishing, gutting its credibility with island nations — China is filling every gap with loans, ports, and infrastructure India and Australia, the paper argues, are better positioned than any other pairing to offer Pacific Island Countries a genuine alternative — development-first, non-interventionist, and built on mutual trust rather than debt traps. India even has a new maritime doctrine for exactly this — MAHASAGAR — announced by PM Modi in Mauritius in March 2025. STORY | Pleas against hate speeches: No legislative vacuum exists warranting intervention, says SC The Supreme Court on Wednesday said the existing framework of criminal law adequately addresses the issue of hate speeches and no "legislative vacuum" exists warranting intervention. "The contention that the field of hate speech remains legislatively unoccupied, is misconceived," a bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta said in its verdict on a batch of petitions related to hate speeches. The top court said it would be open to the Centre and the competent legislative authorities to consider in their wisdom whether any further legislative or policy measures were warranted in light of the evolving societal challenges or to bring about suitable amendments as suggested by the Law Commission's 267th report of March 2017. "While we decline to issue directions of the nature sought, we deem it appropriate to observe that the issues relating to hate speeches and rumour-mongering bear directly upon the preservation of fraternity, dignity and Constitutional order," Justice Nath said while pronouncing the verdict. The apex court said the creation of criminal offences and the prescription of punishments lie squarely with the legislative domain. READ: ptinews.com/story/national/p…

कल रक्षा मंत्री ने, स्पष्ट रूप से प्रधानमंत्री की स्वीकृति और उनके निर्देश पर, बिश्केक में बोलते हुए पाकिस्तान को शर्मनाक क्लीन चिट दे दी। क्या पाकिस्तान आतंकवाद का केंद्र नहीं है? क्या पाकिस्तान में ऐसे आतंकी कैंप नहीं हैं, जिनका निशाना भारत है? क्या पाकिस्तान में भारत-विरोधी सोच को बढ़ावा नहीं दिया जाता? क्या मुंबई और पहलगाम के आतंकी हमलों की साजिश और उन्हें अंजाम पाकिस्तान से जुड़े आतंकियों ने नहीं दिया था? स्पष्ट है कि पाकिस्तान के प्रति यह नया रुख, अमेरिका को खुश करने और चीन के सामने संतुलित समर्पण की प्रधानमंत्री की नीति का ही हिस्सा है। रक्षा मंत्री के ये चौंकाने वाले बयान उतने ही राष्ट्र-विरोधी हैं, जितनी 19 जून 2020 को चीन को लेकर प्रधानमंत्री द्वारा दी गई विचित्र क्लीन चिट थी। Video

रक्षा मंत्री राजनाथ सिंह ने प्रधानमंत्री मोदी के नक्शे-कदम पर चलते हुए, उनके निर्देश पर पाकिस्तान को 'क्लीन चिट' दे दी। जो पाकिस्तान आतंक का सरगना रहा है, जिसके हाथ हिंदुस्तान में मासूमों के खून से रंगे हैं- उसे भारत के रक्षा मंत्री वैश्विक मंच से 'क्लीन चिट' दे रहे हैं। ये बेहद शर्मनाक है। ऐसे में क्या मोदी सरकार मानती है 👇 ⦁ पाकिस्तान में कोई आतंकी कैंप नहीं चलाए जा रहे हैं? ⦁ पाकिस्तान में भारत विरोधी सोच को बढ़ावा नहीं दिया जाता? ⦁ क्या मुंबई और पहलगाम के आतंकी हमलों की साजिश में पाकिस्तान का हाथ नहीं था? साफ है कि ये नरेंद्र मोदी की 'सरेंडर नीति' है, जिसमें वो पाकिस्तान के लिए नरमी दिखाकर, ट्रंप को खुश करना चाहते हैं। रक्षा मंत्री का ये बयान राष्ट्र-विरोधी है, इसके लिए हिंदुस्तान की जनता उन्हें कभी माफ नहीं करेगी। Video

At the recent roundtable on "Protected Cultivation as a Strategy for Crop Diversification and Income Growth", #ICRIER brought together policymakers, researchers, farmers and industry experts to discuss pathways for scaling high-value agriculture in India, and the consensus was clear that the future of Indian agriculture lies beyond wheat and paddy. Setting the context, Dr #AshokGulati, Distinguished Professor, ICRIER, framed the central paradox: if polyhouses can deliver 3–5x higher productivity and 30–50x better income returns than traditional paddy-wheat systems, why does adoption remain near zero? The discussions pointed to what needs to shift: ✅Starting with clustered, high-potential geographies — Bassi-Boraj in Rajasthan and Kutch in Gujarat show what's possible ✅Building financing models that match the investment horizon of polyhouse farming ✅Strengthening FPOs to give smallholders collective market power ✅ Investing in cold chains, logistics, and post-harvest infrastructure The event also marked the launch of ICRIER's report "Augmenting Farmers' Income through Protected Cultivation", authored by Dr Ranjana Roy and Dr #AshokGulati, which makes the case that the shift from cereal-based systems to high-value horticulture won't happen through technology alone, it requires coordinated policy support, better credit access, and a fundamental rethink of how farming systems are designed. Protected cultivation holds transformative potential. Unlocking it will take aligning technology, markets, and policy together. 🔗 Read the full report: icrier.org/publications/augm… #Agriculture #FoodSecurity #ProtectedCultivation #PolicyResearch #ICRIER #AgriTech #FarmerIncome

فدراسیون بین‌المللی فوتبال (فیفا) اعلام کرده است که با تصویب یک اصلاحیه‌ی مهم در مقررات این فدراسیون، تیم ملی فوتبال زنان افغانستان اکنون می‌تواند به نمایندگی از کشور خود در رقابت‌های رسمی بین‌المللی شرکت کند. براساس اعلامیه‌‌ی فیفا، این اصلاحیه دیروز (سه‌شنبه، ۸ ثور) در شورای فیفا تصویب شده است و به این شورا اجازه می‌دهد که در شرایط استثنایی و در مشوره با کنفدراسیون مربوطه، تشکیل و ثبت یک تیم ملی به نمایندگی از یک کشور را ثبت کند. جیانی انفانتینو، رییس فدراسیون بین‌المللی فوتبال گفته است: «این اصلاحیه‌ی مهم بازیکنان زن افغا‌نستان، از جمله اعضای تیم زنان متحد افغانستان که تحت حمایت فیفا است، را قادر می‌سازد که در هماهنگی با کنفدراسیون فوتبال آسیا، به نمایندگی از کشورشان در رقابت‌های بین‌المللی شرکت کنند.» بیشتر بخوانید: storage.googleapis.com/quriu…

I held an expanded meeting on key issues related to the export of Ukrainian weapons. The export of Ukrainian weapons will become a reality – we have approved all the details at the level of our state institutions. Currently, our security expertise and weapons, which have been tested in modern warfare, are of interest to all partners capable of ensuring a real level of protection for their statehood and the lives of their citizens. We have proposed to partners who support Ukraine a special format of cooperation – Drone Deals – special agreements on the production and supply of our drones, missiles, ammunition, and other in-demand types of weapons, military equipment, software, integration with partners’ defense systems, as well as the provision of our expertise and the technological exchange needed by Ukraine. Today, I approved the areas for this interstate work and the development of automatic permits for businesses regarding arms exports. The algorithm is absolutely clear: at the interstate level, based on the principle of reciprocity, we define the framework for security cooperation through the relevant agreement. Then the process continues at the level of state institutions and manufacturers. We are simplifying bureaucratic procedures, maintaining an adequate level of export control, and launching practical operating mechanisms for companies. Ukrainian companies will receive a real opportunity to enter partner countries’ markets, provided that our military has the right to receive the necessary volume of weapons first. A surplus of production capacity in Ukraine for certain types of weapons reaches 50 per cent, and this is a direct result of our state investment in Ukraine’s defense industry and our cooperation with partners. I instructed the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, together with our intelligence services and the Security Service of Ukraine, to determine the list of countries to which exports of our weapons are not possible due to their cooperation with the aggressor state. I travelled through Great Nicobar today. These are the most extraordinary forests I have ever seen in my life. Trees older than memory. Forests that took generations to grow. The people on this island are equally beautiful - both the adivasi communities and the settlers - but they are being robbed of what is rightfully theirs. The government calls what it is doing here a “Project.” What I have seen is not a project. It is millions of trees marked for the axe. It is 160 square kilometres of rainforest condemned to die. It is communities that have been ignored while their homes have been snatched away. This is not development. This is destruction dressed in development’s language. So I will say it plainly, and I will keep saying it: what is being done in Great Nicobar is one of the biggest scams and gravest crimes against this country’s natural and tribal heritage in our lifetime. It must be stopped. And it can be stopped - if Indians choose to see what I have seen. Video

Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif's Message on International Day in Memory of the Victims of Earthquakes, April 29, 2026. Pakistan joins the international community today in expressing solidarity with victims of earthquakes and other natural disasters around the world. Designated by the United Nations, this day serves not only as a reminder to honor those who lost their lives in earthquakes but also to express compassion for survivors and to strengthen global resolve in disaster preparedness and resilience. It reminds us that mitigating the devastating impacts of natural disasters requires improved infrastructure, comprehensive planning, and widespread public awareness. At the global level, this day underscores the importance of international cooperation. Collaborative efforts are essential for advancing early warning technologies and strengthening structural resilience. Integrating safety standards into construction practices can significantly reduce the destruction caused by earthquakes. In Pakistan, the devastating earthquake of October 2005 remains deeply etched in our national memory. Over 80,000 lives were lost, and nearly 3 million people were displaced across Azad Jammu & Kashmir and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. In few moments the tragedy of 2005 earthquake left profound human, social, and economic impacts on our national memory. Yet equally memorable was the resilience, collective resolve and courage of the countrymen which no doubt stand as a powerful testament to the strength of the human spirit. In the aftermath of this catastrophe, Pakistan introduced comprehensive institutional reforms to enhance its disaster management capacity. The establishment of the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) marked a significant milestone in creating a coordinated national framework. While earthquakes cannot be predicted, NDMA utilizes historical trends, fault line data, and geospatial technologies to identify high-risk areas. These efforts support early warning systems, infrastructure, strengthening, preparedness, and damage reduction. In alignment with global initiatives, Pakistan reaffirms its commitment to the United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction (UNDRR) and the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015–2030. And Pakistan emphasizes the need for equitable access to early warning systems and the development of earthquake-resilient infrastructure. At the national level, capacity building and public awareness remain key priorities. These include training of community first responders, integrating disaster education into the curriculum under the Pakistan School Safety Framework (PSSF), and investing in Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and satellite-based modeling. The Government of Pakistan reiterates its commitment to building a safer and more resilient future and calls upon the international community to strengthen collective efforts through shared responsibility and cooperation.

BREAKING 🔴 The United Arab Emirates, OPEC’s 3rd largest oil producer, announced it will leave OPEC and OPEC+ effective May 1. The move would free the UAE from cartel production quotas, allowing it to pump oil at full capacity, set its own export strategy and price crude without group restrictions. That could pave the way for higher UAE output, stronger state revenues and downward pressure on global oil prices. Lower prices and increased supply would likely be welcomed by President Trump, who has long criticized OPEC production limits and called for cheaper energy.

New blog: Vibe Coding Is Becoming an OSINT Risk The biggest #OSINT risk in vibe coding is not that the code might break. It is that the tool might work just well enough to be trusted. That is where the danger begins. A parser silently misses posts. A monitor drops updates. A matching workflow links the wrong people. A summarizer removes uncertainty. A dashboard makes weak assumptions look clean. No crash. No warning. No obvious failure. Just a workflow slowly bending your judgment. In OSINT, tools are not neutral. They shape collection. 🇵🇸 Le Moyne College President Tells Genocide Survivor He Cannot Use the Word “Genocide.” Le Moyne College, a Jesuit institution in Syracuse, New York, sent a letter to students this week condemning the language used by Palestinian poet Mosab Abu Toha during an April 15 guest lecture — specifically his use of the word “genocide” to describe Israel’s actions in Gaza. President Linda LeMura, without naming him, wrote that the word caused “real hurt” to Jewish students and implied its use was incompatible with the college’s commitment to inclusion. She then listed her commitments going forward: dialogue sessions, new guidelines for “deeply charged” campus programming, and a declaration that antisemitism has no place at Le Moyne — describing Abu Toha’s testimony, implicitly, as an example of bigotry requiring institutional guardrails. Abu Toha, who survived Israeli strikes in Gaza, lost over 100 relatives—most of them children—and still carries physical wounds from a 2009 airstrike, called the letter “deeply shameful.” “How dare you tell a person who survived a genocide that they cannot speak about it?” he wrote. “I never once used the word ‘Jewish’ during the entire event. I refuse to conflate the faith of Judaism with the actions of the state of Israel.” “If anyone told you they felt ‘hurt’ because I used the word genocide,” he wrote, “then I ask you: how should I feel? How should my wife feel after losing her father? How should my three children feel after losing their grandfather?“ Mosab Abu Toha (@MosabAbuToha) ****Statement from Mosab Abu Toha in response to LeMoyne College's President's email to students today***** This is deeply shameful. I cannot believe what I am reading. How dare you tell a person who survived a genocide that they cannot speak about it? On April 15, I had the honor of visiting and speaking at Le Moyne College. I spoke about my lived experience in Gaza, shared the family trees of those killed by Israel, and read my poems. I also played the actual recordings of Israeli airstrikes and artillery shelling that I documented myself while on the ground in Gaza. This morning, the President of the college sent out an email condemning my use of the word GENOCIDE when describing these crimes. She claimed that using that word is "antisemitic." She stated that she recognized the "real hurt" that the word caused to Jewish students. Seriously? Are the crimes of the Israeli state representative of all Jewish people? I personally refuse to believe that is the case. It is utterly ridiculous to begin a letter by stating that your institution welcomes the "free exchange of ideas," only to immediately condemn a speaker, not for sharing abstract ideas, but for sharing his own life. I still carry the physical wounds of a 2009 airstrike on my neck, my forehead, and my cheek. My wife and I have lost over one hundred relatives, most of them children. Some of them have still not been buried. Who are these students you are talking about? Not a single person who identified themselves as Jewish approached me after my talk to offer condolences or acknowledge the actual crimes committed against me and my family. I never once used the word "Jewish" during the entire event; I refuse to conflate the faith of Judaism with the actions of the state of Israel. Yet, you suggest my language caused "hurt." Whoever went to your office to complain about my words should have been the first to approach the stage to show humanity and support for a survivor. It may surprise you to know that I used the word GENOCIDE to describe Israel’s actions in Gaza long before most human rights organizations, including prominent Israeli organizations, and leading Holocaust and Genocide scholars arrived at the same conclusion. I hope this fact does not "hurt" anyone even more. If anyone told you they felt "hurt" because I used the word GENOCIDE, then I ask you: how should I feel? How should my wife feel after losing her father? How should my three children feel after losing their grandfather? At a time when a GENOCIDE should be condemned, it is the survivors and those who speak out against it who are being targeted instead. Volodymyr Zelenskyy / Володимир Зеленський (@ZelenskyyUa) I held an expanded meeting on key issues related to the export of Ukrainian weapons. The export of Ukrainian weapons will become a reality – we have approved all the details at the level of our state institutions. Currently, our security expertise and weapons, which have been tested in modern warfare, are of interest to all partners capable of ensuring a real level of protection for their statehood and the lives of their citizens. We have proposed to partners who support Ukraine a special format of cooperation – Drone Deals – special agreements on the production and supply of our drones, missiles, ammunition, and other in-demand types of weapons, military equipment, software, integration with partners’ defense systems, as well as the provision of our expertise and the technological exchange needed by Ukraine. Today, I approved the areas for this interstate work and the development of automatic permits for businesses regarding arms exports. The algorithm is absolutely clear: at the interstate level, based on the principle of reciprocity, we define the framework for security cooperation through the relevant agreement. Then the process continues at the level of state institutions and manufacturers. We are simplifying bureaucratic procedures, maintaining an adequate level of export control, and launching practical operating mechanisms for companies. Ukrainian companies will receive a real opportunity to enter partner countries’ markets, provided that our military has the right to receive the necessary volume of weapons first. A surplus of production capacity in Ukraine for certain types of weapons reaches 50 per cent, and this is a direct result of our state investment in Ukraine’s defense industry and our cooperation with partners. I instructed the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, together with our intelligence services and the Security Service of Ukraine, to determine the list of countries to which exports of our weapons are not possible due to their cooperation with the aggressor state. This is a serious challenge – to prevent our technologies and weapons from falling into Russian hands. The National Security and Defense Council of Ukraine will coordinate export processes and act as a guarantor that the needs of Ukraine’s Defense and Security Forces are met first, while only surplus production – what manufacturers can produce beyond the state order in Ukraine – will be exported. The Ministry of Defense of Ukraine and the General Staff will determine the required volumes for the needs of our Defense Forces. I have instructed government officials and the National Security and Defense Council of Ukraine to present to the public the necessary information on the details of our weapons export process. Провів розширену нараду щодо ключових питань експорту української зброї. Експорт української зброї буде реальним. Ми погодили всі деталі на рівні наших державних інституцій. Наразі наша безпекова експертиза та зброя, що була перевірена сучасною війною, цікава всім партнерам, які спроможні забезпечити собі реальний рівень захисту національної державності та життя людей. Ми запропонували партнерам, які допомагають Україні, особливий формат співпраці Drone Deals – спеціальні угоди щодо виробництва та постачання наших дронів, ракет, снарядів та інших затребуваних видів зброї, бойової техніки, софту, інтеграції з оборонними системами партнерів, а також забезпечення нашої експертизи та потрібного Україні технологічного обміну. Сьогодні затвердив напрями такої міждержавної роботи та опрацювання автоматичних дозволів для бізнесу щодо експорту зброї. Порядок дій абсолютно чіткий: на міждержавному рівні на основі принципу взаємності відповідною угодою визначаємо рамки для безпекової роботи, далі розпочинається процес уже на рівні державних інституцій і виробників. Спрощуємо бюрократичні процедури, зберігаємо достатній рівень експортного контролю та запускаємо практичний зміст для роботи компаній. Українські компанії отримають реальну можливість виходу на ринок країн-партнерів за умови права наших військових узяти необхідний обсяг зброї першими. Профіцит виробничих спроможностей в Україні за деякими видами зброї досягає 50%, і це прямий результат наших державних інвестицій в оборонну промисловість України та нашої співпраці з партнерами. Доручив МЗС України разом з нашими розвідками та СБУ визначити перелік країн, до яких експорт нашої зброї неможливий із причин їхньої співпраці з державою-агресором. Це серйозний виклик – не допустити потрапляння до росіян наших технологій та зразків зброї. РНБО України координуватиме експортні процеси й буде гарантом, що першочергово забезпечуються потреби Сил оборони та безпеки України у зброї, а на експорт відправляється надлишок – те, що виробники можуть зробити понад державне замовлення в Україні. Міністерство оборони України та Генеральний штаб визначатимуть обсяги потреби Сил оборони нашої держави. Доручив урядовцям та РНБО України представити суспільству необхідну інформацію щодо деталей процесу експорту нашої зброї. Слава Україні!

I held an expanded meeting on key issues related to the export of Ukrainian weapons. The export of Ukrainian weapons will become a reality – we have approved all the details at the level of our state institutions. Currently, our security expertise and weapons, which have been tested in modern warfare, are of interest to all partners capable of ensuring a real level of protection for their statehood and the lives of their citizens. We have proposed to partners who support Ukraine a special format of cooperation – Drone Deals – special agreements on the production and supply of our drones, missiles, ammunition, and other in-demand types of weapons, military equipment, software, integration with partners’ defense systems, as well as the provision of our expertise and the technological exchange needed by Ukraine. Today, I approved the areas for this interstate work and the development of automatic permits for businesses regarding arms exports. The algorithm is absolutely clear: at the interstate level, based on the principle of reciprocity, we define the framework for security cooperation through the relevant agreement. Then the process continues at the level of state institutions and manufacturers. We are simplifying bureaucratic procedures, maintaining an adequate level of export control, and launching practical operating mechanisms for companies. Ukrainian companies will receive a real opportunity to enter partner countries’ markets, provided that our military has the right to receive the necessary volume of weapons first. A surplus of production capacity in Ukraine for certain types of weapons reaches 50 per cent, and this is a direct result of our state investment in Ukraine’s defense industry and our cooperation with partners. I instructed the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, together with our intelligence services and the Security Service of Ukraine, to determine the list of countries to which exports of our weapons are not possible due to their cooperation with the aggressor state. This is a serious challenge – to prevent our technologies and weapons from falling into Russian hands. The National Security and Defense Council of Ukraine will coordinate export processes and act as a guarantor that the needs of Ukraine’s Defense and Security Forces are met first, while only surplus production – what manufacturers can produce beyond the state order in Ukraine – will be exported. The Ministry of Defense of Ukraine and the General Staff will determine the required volumes for the needs of our Defense Forces. I have instructed government officials and the National Security and Defense Council of Ukraine to present to the public the necessary information on the details of our weapons export process. Glory to Ukraine!

Important to address the 11th Review Conference of the Parties to the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty in New York today. The #NPT has stood for more than five decades and commands the widest adherence of any treaty in this domain. Its 191 Parties bring together countries with and without nuclear weapons, united by a shared responsibility. This is a very particular moment. The risk of nuclear disaster has risen to levels not seen since the height of the Cold War. War has returned to Europe and the Middle East, and the multilateral frameworks underpinning peace and security are under immense strain. In today’s nuclear domain, we face a precarious standoff, with more actors, more risks, and less clarity. Preventing nuclear proliferation is in our common interest, and the NPT is our most powerful multilateral instrument. At the heart of this effort is the @IAEAorg’s safeguards regime, ensuring that nuclear material is not diverted from peaceful to military use through a firm, fair and impartial verification system. At the same time, nuclear science and technology have enormous benefits for humankind and should be shared more widely. Through the Agency, these benefits support energy and food security, healthcare and environmental protection around the world. Today, we are here because we have one job to do: to ensure that the NPT and the IAEA remain strong, not in spite of today’s turmoil, but precisely because of it. #RevCon #NPTRevCon

Less bureaucracy. More presence in the field. Stronger African representation in int'l organizations. That was my response during the high-level session “Africa Leads the Future of Health” at the @WorldHealthSmt in Nairobi, when the moderator asked what multilaterals must change for African leadership to become real in practice. I also shared how @WHO_Europe is trying to do its part - involving an African representative in our newly established Scientific Advisory Board and inviting several African countries to join our Small Countries Initiative. One question from the audience captured the spirit of the discussion: if Africa is encouraged to be in the driving seat, what does it take to be a good driver? I answered with something my wife often tells me: a good driver is not the one who drives fast, but the one who drives safely. In this context, safe driving means having a clear destination in mind, having strong and confident leadership behind the wheel, and building partnerships that help countries move forward together.

The exam, which focused on the laws of mourning, is part of the series of tests on Jewish law taken by rabbinical candidates. The Chief Rabbinate, which is Orthodox, does not offer ordination to women, but those who pass the tests are eligible for other state benefits. The UAE's decision to leave OPEC is the most significant blow it has dealt to Saudi Arabia and the entire GCC since the Saudi Emirati rivalry. Thus far, Saudi Arabia has avoided responding to UAE provocations but may not be able to after this. The OPEC issue is significant but has been overshadowed by other geopolitical issues. Saudi Arabia, the de facto leader of OPEC cartel, has kept production low for some time to keep prices up, producing 9 million barrels per day while the UAE was allocated 2.9 million. The UAE wanted to increase to 3.7 million. Saudis need inflated oil prices, at least 86 dollars per barrel, to avoid budget deficits and sustain their welfare state and economic transition under Vision 2030. The Emirates, by contrast, have a more diverse economy. With the UAE, OPEC's third largest producer at 15 percent, leaving, the group will struggle to maintain its monopoly over global oil supply and thus prices. The Emirates will eventually join the US, which intends to liberalise the oil market while positioning itself as a major producer. This will further strain US ties with the Saudi led GCC (without UAE), since all GCC economies except the UAE are heavily dependent on oil revenues. The logical continuation of this step will likely lead to the UAE's expulsion from the GCC and Arab League, accelerating a new order in the Middle East and broader Muslim world.

A Polícia Federal deflagrou nesta terça duas grandes operações de combate ao crime: uma contra um esquema bilionário no porto do Rio de Janeiro e outra, de dimensão internacional, contra o abuso sexual de crianças e adolescentes. Em ação conjunta da Polícia Federal, Receita Federal e Ministério Público Federal, no Rio de Janeiro e no Espírito Santo, são cumpridos 45 mandados de busca e apreensão para desarticular um esquema de facilitação de contrabando e liberação irregular de mercadorias importadas, que movimentou mais de R$ 86 bilhões. Dezessete auditores fiscais e oito analistas tributários foram afastados. Também há bloqueio de bens e restrições a atividades de nove despachantes. Já na operação em defesa de crianças e adolescentes, mais de 500 policiais federais atuam em todos os estados e em articulação com forças de segurança estaduais e de outros 15 países. São 159 mandados de busca e apreensão e 16 de prisão preventiva, com foco na identificação e prisão de autores de crimes de abuso sexual, muitos deles potencializados pelo ambiente digital. Só em 2026, a Polícia Federal já cumpriu mais de 450 mandados de prisão contra foragidos por crimes sexuais. Por ações como esta que nós fortalecemos a PF. Na última semana, anunciamos a contratação de 1000 novos policiais. Seguimos firmes no enfrentamento ao crime e na proteção da sociedade brasileira.

1. London Marathon 2026 saw Sabastian Sawe & Yomif Kejelcha shatter the 2-hour barrier. Sawe reset the world record for men’s, while Tigst Assefa set a new women’s world record, beating her own best. #CutTheClutter explains the significance of these achievements, how science & tech are fuelling ambition in sports & the super shoe race. 2. Sawe’s run took 1:59:30, shaving off a full 65 seconds from the existing record set up in Chicago in 2023 by Kelvin Kiptum (2:00:35). That is incredible in itself, but the London marathon was really special — No.2 (Yomif Kejelcha) & No.3 (Jacob Kiplimo) also broke the world record. Assefa, at 2:15:41, shaved 9 seconds off her own record. 3. This is the 4th time since 2014 that the world marathon record has been reset, &, in this time, the record has been cut by 3 minutes 37 seconds. Think about it: 42.2km in less than 120 minutes. So, Sawe & Kejelcha averaged less than 3 minutes/km. It’s a story of endurance, of strength, of the science of long-distance running & technology. 4. This is the era of super shoes — a great tussle between the world’s greatest runners is also described as the athletic equivalent of an arms race between Adidas & Nike. New tech is coming in. Carbon composites are coming in. Shoes are getting lighter & lighter. 5. Then, of course, there’s the nutrition element. Every gram of carbohydrate consumed while running is monitored. Sawe, through his run, was consuming carbohydrate at 115g/hour. Before the run, he was given a shot of sodium bicarbonate to help prevent a lactic acid buildup in his muscles. 6. India’s most durable track record stood in the name of Shivnath Singh. In 1978, when he was a Hawaldar in the Army’s Bihar regiment, Singh set a record in Jalandhar of 2:12:00. This remained unchallenged for 48 years, until 2 weeks ago, when another Indian Army runner, Sawan Barwal, shaved 2 seconds off Singh’s record. 7. According to preliminary reports, an important high-level command meeting was taking place at the site — involving officers who directly coordinated Kalibr missile strikes on Ukrainian cities. The headquarters that had directed missiles at homes, schools, and hospitals for years was reportedly destroyed. Sources claim this was the work of a unit of the Main Directorate of Intelligence of Ukraine known as the “Madyar Wolves,” under the personal command of Serhii Mahera. The fighters allegedly infiltrated a deeply rear, well-protected facility, planted powerful charges, and detonated them precisely during the meeting. The explosion was reportedly so powerful that almost nothing of the headquarters remained. According to unconfirmed reports, several admirals and senior officers of the Black Sea Fleet were among those killed.

In any normal country, purchasing stolen goods is an act that entails legal liability. This applies, in particular, to grain stolen by Russia. Another vessel carrying such grain has arrived at a port in Israel and is preparing to unload. This is not – and cannot be – legitimate business. The Israeli authorities cannot be unaware of which ships are arriving at the country’s ports and what cargo they are carrying. Russia is systematically seizing grain on temporarily occupied Ukrainian land and organizing its export through individuals linked to the occupiers. Such schemes violate the laws of the State of Israel itself. Ukraine has taken all necessary steps through diplomatic channels to prevent such incidents. However, we see that yet another such vessel has not been stopped. I have instructed the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine to inform all partners of our state about the situation. Based on information from our intelligence services, Ukraine is preparing a relevant sanctions package that will cover both those directly transporting this grain and the individuals and legal entities attempting to profit from this criminal scheme. We will also coordinate with European partners to ensure that the relevant individuals are included in European sanctions regimes. Ukraine counts on partnership and mutual respect with every state. We are genuinely working to enhance security, particularly in the Middle East region. We expect that the Israeli authorities will respect Ukraine and refrain from actions that undermine our bilateral relations.

Important to address the 11th Review Conference of the Parties to the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty in New York today. The #NPT has stood for more than five decades and commands the widest adherence of any treaty in this domain. Its 191 Parties bring together countries with and without nuclear weapons, united by a shared responsibility. This is a very particular moment. The risk of nuclear disaster has risen to levels not seen since the height of the Cold War. War has returned to Europe and the Middle East, and the multilateral frameworks underpinning peace and security are under immense strain. In today’s nuclear domain, we face a precarious standoff, with more actors, more risks, and less clarity. Preventing nuclear proliferation is in our common interest, and the NPT is our most powerful multilateral instrument. At the heart of this effort is the @IAEAorg’s safeguards regime, ensuring that nuclear material is not diverted from peaceful to military use through a firm, fair and impartial verification system. At the same time, nuclear science and technology have enormous benefits for humankind and should be shared more widely. Through the Agency, these benefits support energy and food security, healthcare and environmental protection around the world. Today, we are here because we have one job to do: to ensure that the NPT and the IAEA remain strong, not in spite of today’s turmoil, but precisely because of it. #RevCon #NPTRevCon

The Special ASEAN Ministers on Energy Meeting (AMEM) on the Latest Situation in the Middle East was convened on 27 April 2026 via virtual platform, under the Chairmanship of H.E. Sharon S. Garin, Secretary of the Department of Energy of the Republic of the Philippines. The Meeting brought together ASEAN Energy Ministers and representatives, supported by Senior Officials, ASEAN Secretariat, ASEAN Centre for Energy (ACE), ASEAN Council on Petroleum and Energy (ASCOPE) and relevant regional energy bodies. The Deputy Secretary-General of ASEAN for the ASEAN Economic Community, H.E. Satvinder Singh, was also in the Meeting. The Meeting urged the expeditious completion of national processes towards its ratification of the ASEAN Framework Agreement on Petroleum Security (APSA), and noted ongoing efforts to prepare emergency response arrangements. The Meeting also underscored the importance of closer engagement with Dialogue Partners to strengthen regional preparedness and response capacity. The Meeting commenced with opening remarks by the Chair, followed by a briefing from the ASEAN Secretariat on the ASEAN Foreign Ministers’ and ASEAN Economic Ministers’ Statements regarding the situation in the Middle East, as well as updates on the APSA, providing a cross-sectoral perspective on the broader geopolitical and economic context and its potential impacts on regional stability, supply chains, and economic activities. The Chair of the ASEAN Senior Officials Meeting on Energy (SOME) further presented key outcomes and recommendations from Ad Hoc SOME Preparatory Meeting on 24 April 2026, highlighting developments in regional energy security and the way forward. The Meeting also benefitted from insights by the International Energy Agency on the global energy situation and by the ASEAN Centre for Energy on the regional energy situation and proposed actions of the Coordinated Emergency Response Mechanism (CERM) under APSA. Ministers subsequently exchanged views on national preparedness, contingency measures, and policy responses to potential supply disruptions, while underscoring the importance of strengthened regional coordination and collective action to enhance ASEAN’s energy resilience and maintain stable, secure, and affordable energy supplies amid global uncertainties. The Meeting concluded with the adoption of the Joint Statement, reaffirming ASEAN’s coordinated approach and resolve to safeguard regional energy security. As ASEAN navigates an increasingly complex global energy landscape, continued collaboration, closer engagement with Dialogue Partners, and timely information-sharing will remain essential in ensuring a resilient and responsive regional energy system. 1. Can you read #WritingsontheWall in poll-bound West Bengal without even stepping into Kolkata? Most certainly you can. And that’s just what I did about a week before the phase 1 voting. So, come with me 600km from the state capital to Siliguri Corridor. To be more precise, we begin at Naxalbari. ￼ 2. If anybody kept track of these things anymore, we would now be observing the beginning of the 60th year of the armed Maoist uprising that began here this week in 1967. As it happens, I found 2 old comrades in Bengai Jot busy giving a fresh coat of paint & a scrub to a memorial to the lost revolution. 3. The memorial has busts of Marx, Lenin, Engels, Stalin, Mao, Charu Majumdar & Saroj Dutta. And…Lin Biao, the strongman boss of Chinese PLA & Mao’s heir, branded a traitor after his mysterious death in 1971. In Naxalbari, I found a wallpaper declaring (translated from Bangla): There is no liberation through votes. Liberation is only through revolution. 4. Naxalbari is where the revolution rose. It’s also where it lies buried. In 2021, BJP won the seat. This time, there was a 92% turnout. This is when the latest avatar of the Naxals in east-central India has been entombed. In Kerala, the Left fights double incumbency. And, unless it pulls off a surprise on May 4, we could proclaim the conclusive marginalisation of all Left in our independent history. ￼ 5. Now Naxalbari is mostly forgotten but Siliguri is top of the mind. The BJP has made its vulnerability a key electoral plank, linking it to demographic change & dovetailing it neatly into its Hindu- Muslim polarisation pitch. This infiltration-demographic change-national security-polarisation is a dominant strain in BJP’s campaign. Development takes second place. 6. The one area where BJP does not have an answer to the Trinamool Congress is leadership. While Mamata Banerjee is a Bengali titan & probably the hardest, the most skillful campaigner in India today, BJP, true to its recent approach, is not projecting an obvious leader. It doesn’t have one either in Bengal. 7. One interesting (and, dare I say, Mamata) thing I saw at a rally was 2 women in uniform. Not police, not paramilitary, not a uniform I could recognise. What was written on their shoulder was WINNER. A 5-minute conversation tells us the story. The BJP’s big criticism of Mamata Banerjee has been over women’s safety. So, she created a specialised female cadre within her police force only to look after women’s security. ￼ 8. Where rural populations cannot save, borrow, or insure against risk, agricultural productivity stagnates – and with it, broader economic growth. In #Benin, where agriculture accounts for 70% of employment and 30% of GDP, IFAD has worked to address this gap through sustained investment in rural financial inclusion. The IFAD-financed Adapted Rural Financial Services Development Project extended savings and credit services to more than 50,000 rural people. As a result, supported households were significantly more likely to hold savings (88% vs. 67%) and to access loans (56% vs. 34%) than those in non-supported areas. The project also strengthened the Association of Financial Services of Benin (ASF), a community-based microfinance network, ensuring that services remained reliable, regulation-compliant and accessible well beyond the project's closure. Building on these results, a new IFAD-financed intervention has already delivered measurable early outcomes – a 150% increase in local seed production, expanded agricultural insurance coverage and a projected 3,000+ jobs along horticultural value chains. اسلام آباد : 28 اپریل، 2026. وزیراعظم محمد شہباز شریف نے ملک میں سرمایہ کاری کے فروغ پر جائزہ اجلاس کی صدارت کی. اجلاس سے گفتگو کرتے ہوئے وزیرِ اعظم نے کہا کہ ملک میں اقتصادی ترقی کیلئے سرمایہ کاری کا فروغ حکومت کی اولین ترجیح ہے. برآمدات بڑھانے کے لیے ملکی اور غیر ملکی سرمایہ کاروں کو تمام ضروری سہولیات کی فراہمی یقینی بنائی جائے. وزیرِ اعظم نے ہدیات کی کہ سرمایہ کاری کے فروغ کیلئے ریگولیٹری تعمیل پر عملدرآمد کو مزید آسان اور کم خرچ بنایا جائے. حکومت اور سرمایہ کاروں کے درمیان رابطوں کو مضبوط کیا جائے، لائسنسنگ اور دیگر سروسز تک رسائی کے سارے نظام کی ڈیجیٹائزیشن کی رفتار تیز کی جائے. وزیرِ اعظم نے مزید کہا کہ خصوصی سرمایہ کاری سہولت کونسل کے قیام سے ملک میں سرمایہ کاروں کے اعتماد میں اضافہ ہوا ہے. اجلاس کو ملک میں سرمایہ کاری میں اضافے کے حوالےسے حکومتی اقدامات پر بریفنگ دی گئی. بریفنگ میں بتایا گیا کہ رواں مالی سال جولائی سے مارچ تک ملکی برآمدات میں خصوصی اقتصادی زونز کا حصہ 3.7 فیصد رہا. مالی سال 2028 تک ملکی برآمدات میں خصوصی اکنامک زونز کا حصہ 8 فیصد تک لیجانے کا حدف رکھا گیا ہے. صوبوں کی مشاورت سے سرمایہ کاری کے فروغ کے لیے بزنس-ریڈی ایکشن پلان تیار کیا جا رہا ہے. اجلاس کو مزید بتایا گیا کہ سرمایہ کاروں اور کاروباری حضرات کے لئے حکومتی اجازت ناموں کے حصول آسان بنانے کیلئے تمام سروسز ڈیجیٹائز کی جا رہی ہیں، جس کے لئے پاکستان ریگولیٹری رجسٹری قائم کی جا رہی ہے. ملک میں اس وقت 21 خصوصی اقتصادی زونز آپریشنل ہیں اور جون 2026 تک یہ تعداد 26 ہو جائے گی. آسان کاروبار ایکٹ کے تحت سرخ فیتے کا خاتمہ ہوگا اور ڈیجیٹل سروسز کی فراہمی سے سرمایہ کاری میں مزید سہولت فراہم ہو گی. اجلاس میں وفاقی وزیر قانون و انصاف اعظم نذیر تارڑ ،وفاقی وزیر اقتصادی امور احد خان چیمہ ، وفاقی وزیر انفارمیشن ٹیکنالوجی و ٹیلی کام شزا فاطمہ ، وزیر مملکت برائے خزانہ و ریلوے بلال اظہر کیانی، وزیراعظم کے معاون خصوصی ہارون اختر اور متعلقہ اعلیٰ سرکاری افسران نے شرکت کی ۔ Video

Chhattisgarh, located in central India, is known for its rich tribal heritage, dense forests, and diverse natural landscapes, where waterfalls, caves, and ancient temples create a beautiful blend of nature and history. Beyond its well-known attractions, the state’s lesser-known destinations offer untouched beauty, indigenous traditions, and offbeat experiences. From national parks and hill plateaus to heritage monuments and pilgrimage centres, Chhattisgarh offers a unique confluence of eco, cultural, and spiritual tourism. With a growing emphasis on sustainable and community-based tourism, complemented by traditional crafts, festivals, and simple regional cuisine, Chhattisgarh is emerging as an authentic and unexplored travel destination. Придбання вкраденого в усіх нормальних країнах є діянням, яке тягне за собою юридичну відповідальність. Це стосується, зокрема, і вкраденого Росією зерна. Ще одне судно з таким зерном прибуло в порт Ізраїлю та готується до розвантаження. Це не є і не може бути чистим бізнесом. Влада Ізраїлю не може не знати, які судна та з яким вантажем прибувають у порти країни. Росія систематично забирає зерно на тимчасово окупованій українській землі та організовує вивезення такого зерна особами, які з окупантами пов’язані. Такі оборудки порушують законодавство самої Держави Ізраїль. Україна зробила всі необхідні кроки дипломатичними каналами, щоб унеможливити подібні інциденти. Втім, ми бачимо, що й чергове таке судно не зупинене. Доручив МЗС України поінформувати всіх партнерів нашої держави про ситуацію. Україна на основі інформації від наших розвідок готує відповідний санкційний пакет, який буде охоплювати й тих, хто безпосередньо перевозить це зерно, і тих фізичних та юридичних осіб, хто намагається заробляти на такій кримінальній схемі. Скоординуємо і з європейськими партнерами, щоб відповідні особи були включені у європейські санкційні режими. Україна розраховує на партнерські відносини та взаємну повагу з кожною державою. Ми реально працюємо на те, щоб безпеки, зокрема і в регіоні Близького Сходу, було більше. Очікуємо, що влада Ізраїлю поважатиме Україну й не робитиме кроків, які послаблюють двосторонні відносини.

In any normal country, purchasing stolen goods is an act that entails legal liability. This applies, in particular, to grain stolen by Russia. Another vessel carrying such grain has arrived at a port in Israel and is preparing to unload. This is not – and cannot be – legitimate business. The Israeli authorities cannot be unaware of which ships are arriving at the country’s ports and what cargo they are carrying. Russia is systematically seizing grain on temporarily occupied Ukrainian land and organizing its export through individuals linked to the occupiers. Such schemes violate the laws of the State of Israel itself. Ukraine has taken all necessary steps through diplomatic channels to prevent such incidents. However, we see that yet another such vessel has not been stopped. I have instructed the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine to inform all partners of our state about the situation. Based on information from our intelligence services, Ukraine is preparing a relevant sanctions package that will cover both those directly transporting this grain and the individuals and legal entities attempting to profit from this criminal scheme. We will also coordinate with European partners to ensure that the relevant individuals are included in European sanctions regimes. Ukraine counts on partnership and mutual respect with every state. We are genuinely working to enhance security, particularly in the Middle East region. We expect that the Israeli authorities will respect Ukraine and refrain from actions that undermine our bilateral relations.

As public health leaders, we will be judged by one measure: how we used technology and AI to improve health for all, everywhere. At the World Health Summit in Nairobi, I joined a ministerial session on sovereignty in health data, digital health and AI. The discussion centred on trust: who uses health data, for what purpose, and with what benefit for people. These questions are highly relevant for the European Region too, where over 90% of Member States report legal uncertainty around responsibility for AI use. Both regions have progress to build on and gaps to close. That is why I believe interregional collaboration can bring real value. The discussion made one thing clear: digital health and AI must be matched by clear governance, trained health workers, strong infrastructure and public trust. Otherwise, their promise will remain out of reach. #WHSNairobi2026
